summary:
Space Archive: Forgotten on the Moon and Mars

What happens to spacecraft after their missions end?

Space Archive is an interactive 3D educational platform that brings the history of human exploration on the Moon and Mars to life by documenting the spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments that remain on their surfaces.

Unlike traditional lists and static mission archives, Space Archive allows users to explore planetary environments, discover the locations of historical missions, and follow humanity's exploration journey through an interactive chronological timeline.

Users can select individual objects, approach their locations through smooth camera movement, and explore information about each mission, including its purpose, historical background, and scientific contribution.

By transforming mission history into an immersive visual experience, Space Archive makes planetary exploration easier to understand and helps preserve the scientific legacy of missions that continue to shape our understanding of other worlds.

Our vision is simple: Every mission leaves a story. No discovery should be forgotten
details:
Space Archive: Forgotten on the Moon and Mars

What remains on the Moon and Mars after a space mission ends?

Space Archive is an interactive educational project that explores the history of human-made objects left on the surfaces of the Moon and Mars. It brings together spacecraft, lunar modules, landers, rovers, scientific instruments, and other equipment from important space missions.

The project transforms mission history into a visual 3D exploration experience. Instead of simply reading lists of missions, users can discover different objects, learn when and why they were sent, and understand their role in expanding human knowledge of other worlds.

The archive covers key milestones in planetary exploration, from the early Surveyor and Apollo missions to Mars missions such as Viking, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, InSight, and Ingenuity.

Our goal is to make space exploration history more accessible, engaging, and memorable. By connecting historical missions with their lasting presence on other worlds, Space Archive highlights the scientific and technological legacy of humanity's journey beyond Earth.

The project uses 3D models created or prepared with Blender and a modular software structure for organizing mission data, visual scenes, interface elements, and the chronological timeline.

Every mission leaves something behind. Every object tells a story
